TF-Attack: Transferable and Fast Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models

In this paper, the authors propose a new method called TF-A TTACK for adversarial attacks on large language models (LLMs). The method employs an external third-party overseer to identify important units within sentences, allowing for parallel substitutions of attacks. This approach significantly reduces the time of the attacking process, resulting in a significant speed improvement. The authors also introduce two tricks, Multi-Disturb and Dynamic-Disturb, to enhance the attack effectiveness and transferability. The proposed method is evaluated on six widely adopted benchmarks and shows improved performance compared to existing methods. The authors also demonstrate the transferability of the proposed method and its ability to maintain language fluency.

Keywords: adversarial attacks, large language models, transferability, speed improvement, multi-disturb, dynamic-disturb.

Related Work:

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in adversarial attacks against large language models (LLMs) due to their increasing use in various applications. Previous works have primarily focused on developing adversarial attack methods that are transferable and efficient. However, these methods have limited transferability and are slow, particularly when applied to LLMs.

One of the main limitations of previous methods is the poor transferability of adversarial samples generated by different models. As shown in Table 1, the attack success rate of samples generated from one model and evaluated on another model is low. This highlights the need for a method that can generate adversarial samples that are more transferable across different models.

Another limitation of previous methods is the slow speed of the attack process. As shown in Figure 3, over 80% of the processing time is spent on sequential word-by-word operations when attacking LLMs. This makes it difficult to apply adversarial attacks to real-world applications where speed is a critical factor.

To address these limitations, we propose a new scheme called TF-ATTACK, which employs an external third-party overseer to identify important units within sentences and introduces the concept of Importance Level to perform parallel substitutions of attacks. This approach markedly reduces the time of the attacking process and results in significant speed improvements. Additionally, we employ two tricks, Multi-Disturb and Dynamic-Disturb, to enhance the attack effectiveness and transferability of generated adversarial samples.

Our proposed method, TF-ATTACK, surpasses previous methods in transferability and delivers significant speed improvements, as shown in the experimental results on six widely adopted benchmarks. The results demonstrate that TF-ATTACK maintains a comparable consistency and achieves a comparable level of language fluency that does not cause much confusion for humans. Moreover, the transferability of TF-ATTACK is markedly better than that of BERT-Attack, demonstrating its robustness in migrating attacks across different models.
